final_proof:
Let
\[
h=\frac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr).
\]
All the operations in this definition are pointwise, so for every \(s\in S\),
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(f(s)+g(s)+|f(s)-g(s)|\bigr).
\]
Fix an arbitrary \(s\in S\), and write \(a=f(s)\) and \(b=g(s)\).

If \(a\ge b\), then \(a-b\ge0\), and hence \(|a-b|=a-b\). Therefore
\[
h(s)=\frac12(a+b+a-b)=a=\max\{a,b\}=(f\vee g)(s).
\]
If \(a<b\), then \(a-b<0\), and hence \(|a-b|=-(a-b)=b-a\). Therefore
\[
h(s)=\frac12(a+b+b-a)=b=\max\{a,b\}=(f\vee g)(s).
\]
These two cases exhaust all possibilities for the real numbers \(a,b\). Thus \(h(s)=(f\vee g)(s)\) for every \(s\in S\). Since both \(h\) and \(f\vee g\) are functions with domain \(S\) and codomain \(\mathbb R\), equality at every point of \(S\) implies equality of the functions. Consequently,
\[
f\vee g=\frac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr).
\]
